title: Tougeron correction from an ideal bound on maximal Jacobian minors
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal such that $(R,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and let $N\geq c\geq0$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For $a\in R^N$, let $\Delta(a)\subseteq R$ be the ideal generated by the evaluations at $a$ of all $c\times c$ minors of the matrix $(\partial f_j/\partial x_k)_{j,k}$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative, def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. If $h\geq0$ and $n>2h$ are integers, $f_j(a)\in I^n$ for every $j$, and $I^h\subseteq\Delta(a)$, then there is $b\in R^N$ such that $f_j(b)=0$ for every $j$ and $b_k-a_k\in I^{n-h}$ for every $k$. The ideal power $I^0$ is $R$ and the unique minor for $c=0$ is $1$.

source.place: Elkik II, Lemma 2 (Tougeron), printed pp.561–562; read online 2026-10-24, archival copy WANTED. No exact Stacks tag for this assertion.

proof.text: If $c=0$, take $b=a$. If $I^h=0$, then $I^n=0$ since $n>2h$, so again take $b=a$. Otherwise assume $c>0$ and $I^h\ne0$. By the definition of Noetherian choose a finite generating family $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ of $I^h$. Put $M=(\partial f_j/\partial x_k)(a)$, a $c\times N$ matrix. The hypotheses say that each $t_i$ is a finite linear combination of the maximal minors of $M$.

source.place: Elkik II, Lemma 2 (Tougeron), printed pp.561–562, read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For a set $S$ of $c$ columns, let $M_S$ be the corresponding square matrix, $\delta_S=\det(M_S)$, and $E_S:R^c\to R^N$ the inclusion into those coordinates in the same order. The cited adjugate identity gives $M E_S\operatorname{adj}(M_S)=\delta_S1_c$. Write $t_i=\sum_S\lambda_{iS}\delta_S$ and set $N_i=\sum_S\lambda_{iS}E_S\operatorname{adj}(M_S)$. Thus $N_i$ is an $N\times c$ matrix and $MN_i=t_i1_c$. This uses no division and allows zero-divisors among the $t_i$ and minors.

source.place: Elkik II, Lemma 2 (Tougeron), printed pp.561–562, read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $s=n-2h\ge1$ and write $F=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)^t$. Since $I^n=I^{2h}I^s=(t_it_j:1\le i,j\le r)I^s$, choose column vectors $\alpha_{ij}\in(I^s)^c$ with $F(a)=\sum_{i,j}t_it_j\alpha_{ij}$. This is simply the definition of ideal product: expand each coefficient in a finite sum of products, then expand both factors from $I^h$ in the generators $t_i$.

source.place: Elkik II, Lemma 2 (Tougeron), printed pp.561–562, read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text:
Introduce independent column vectors $U_i=(U_{i1},\ldots,U_{iN})^t$ and expand each monomial of $F(a+\sum_it_iU_i)$ by distributivity. The terms selecting no $U$ give $F(a)$; those selecting exactly one give $\sum_it_iMU_i$, by the explicit monomial formula for partial derivatives. In every remaining term select two of its $U$ factors, with block indices $i,j$, and factor out their scalars $t_it_j$. Group these terms, in a fixed order, into column-vector polynomials $Q_{ij}(U)$ to obtain the identity
$$F(a+\sum_it_iU_i)=F(a)+\sum_it_iMU_i+\sum_{i,j}t_it_jQ_{ij}(U).$$
Every monomial of each $Q_{ij}$ still has total degree at least two in $U$. This is a finite monomial expansion over $R$; no factorial is inverted.

source.place: Elkik II, Lemma 2 (Tougeron), printed pp.561–562, read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text:
Define $N$-component polynomial vectors
$$G_i(U)=U_i+\sum_jN_j(\alpha_{ij}+Q_{ij}(U)).$$
Multiplication by $t_iM$, followed by summation over $i$, gives
$$\sum_it_iMG_i(U)=F(a+\sum_it_iU_i),$$
using $MN_j=t_j1_c$ and the preceding two identities. Regard all $G_i$ together as $m=rN$ equations in the $m$ variables $U_{ik}$. Their constant vector lies in $(I^s)^m$, and their Jacobian at $U=0$ is the identity: the only positive-degree terms besides $U$ have degree at least two.

source.place: Elkik II, Lemma 2 (Tougeron), printed pp.561–562, read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text:
Let $d(U)$ be the determinant of the $m\times m$ Jacobian matrix of $G$. Thus $d(0)=1$. Form
$$B=R[U_1,\ldots,U_m,v]/(G_1,\ldots,G_m,vd(U)-1).$$
Here the single indices enumerate all the previous block coordinates. The full Jacobian matrix of these $m+1$ equations has upper-right column zero, upper-left block $DG$, and bottom-right entry $d$. Expanding its determinant along the last column gives $d^2$. In $B$, $d$ is a unit with inverse $v$, so $d^2$ is a unit. This is a standard smooth presentation by the cited definition. The standard-smooth-is-smooth node therefore says that $B$ is a smooth $R$-algebra.

source.place: Tag 00T6 (definition-standard-smooth); Tag 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth), part (1); explicit auxiliary presentation for Elkik II Lemma 2.

proof.text: Since $s\ge1$, evaluation $U\mapsto0$, $v\mapsto1$ defines an $R$-algebra map $B\to R/I$: all $G_i(0)$ lie in $I^s\subseteq I$ and $d(0)=1$. Apply smooth-algebra lifting with base ring $R$, smooth algebra $S=B$, target algebra $A=R$, and the original ideal $I$. Its hypotheses are precisely the smoothness established above and the given henselian pair $(R,I)$. The lifted map $B\to R$ gives a tuple $u\in I^m$ satisfying $G(u)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0H74 (lemma-lift-smooth-henselian), applied to the explicit auxiliary smooth algebra; Elkik II Lemma 2 final paragraph, p.562.

proof.text: Write $G(U)=U+C+H(U)$, with $C\in(I^s)^m$ and every monomial of $H$ of degree at least two. If $u\in(I^q)^m$, then $H(u)\in(I^{2q})^m$, so $G(u)=0$ implies $u=-C-H(u)\in(I^{\min(s,2q)})^m$. Starting with $q=1$, induction gives $u\in(I^{\min(s,2^e)})^m$ for every $e\ge0$. Choose $e$ with $2^e\ge s$; then $u\in(I^s)^m$. This finite induction neither passes to a completion nor presumes that the pair for the smaller ideal $I^s$ is henselian.

source.place: Elkik II, Lemma 2 (Tougeron), printed pp.561–562, read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Restore the blocks $u_i\in(I^s)^N$ and put $b=a+\sum_it_iu_i$. The identity of Step 5 gives $F(b)=\sum_it_iMG_i(u)=0$. Each coordinate of $b-a$ belongs to $I^hI^s=I^{h+s}=I^{n-h}$, as required. When $h=0$ the same construction uses a generating family of $I^0=R$ (one may take $t_1=1$); it still has $s=n\ge1$. The zero ring, $I=0$, and the empty-equation case were covered in Step 1.

source.place: Elkik II, Lemma 2 (Tougeron), printed pp.561–562, read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

reviewed.note:
mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q116-815ef0cbb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all nine steps in full. The statement is unchanged, it matches Elkik II Lemma 2 (Tougeron), and there are no new nodes. The steps are proved, not just cited:
- Step 2: the adjugate identity gives M N_i = t_i·1 with no division.
- Step 3: F(a) = Σ t_i t_j α_ij with α_ij in I^s, where s = n-2h.
- Step 4: the explicit Taylor expansion uses the monomial derivative formula, so it holds in any characteristic.
- Step 5: Σ t_i M G_i = F(a + Σ t_i U_i), checked by hand, and the Jacobian of G at 0 is the identity.
- Step 6: B = R[U,v]/(G, vd-1) is standard smooth in the sense of the 00T6 node (which allows n = c), with Jacobian determinant d² by block expansion, so the 00T7 node makes it smooth.
- Step 7: the 0H74 lift exists. I checked it against more-algebra.tex line 3440 with S = B, A = R and ideal I.
- Step 8: iterating u ∈ I^s + I^{2q} gives u ∈ I^s without needing I^s henselian.
- Step 9: F(b) = 0 and b-a ∈ I^{n-h}.
The edge cases c = 0, I^h = 0, c > N (where Δ = 0) and h = 0 all hold. Elkik has no local copy (recorded as WANTED), but the proof is self-contained from Stacks nodes. A dereferenced grep for Tougeron finds only the item and its parent, so there is no duplicate.
